column1: # Expected divergences between the reference and the port, per stage oracle.
# A structure listed here is allowed to differ; EVERY OTHER structure must match
# exactly. This file is the whole point of the arrangement: a deliberate
# divergence has to be named, justified and bounded, and it cannot quietly grow
# to cover a second structure because someone could not make the second one
# match.
# `equivalence.sh stage index` reports three classes and they are all printed:
#     match      identical to the reference
#     DIVERGED   differs, and is listed here -> expected
#     FAIL       differs, and is NOT listed here -> a bug
# plus the inverse check:
#     STALE      listed here but actually identical -> the divergence is gone,
#                remove the row (otherwise the list rots into a mute list)
# columns:  stage  structure  finding  corpora  notes
#   corpora: a comma-separated list, or "*" for all. Naming corpora matters:
#            on SIRV the Finding 22 divergence is expected to be EMPTY, because
#            every SIRV part has exactly one active gene.
stage
index
column5: the port fills every active gene; the reference uses a leaked loop variable. On SIRV this must still MATCH - 22 of 22 sites there have a single active gene - so SIRV is the control and droso is the test.
